title: Common Mistakes in Discipleship
description: A lesson on common mistakes in discipleship and how to avoid them in order to effectively guide others in their spiritual journey.

cards.heading: Being Too Aggressive
cards.scriptureText: Let your conversation be always full of grace.
cards.body: Forcing or rushing people can push them away. Discipleship should be done with patience, grace, and sensitivity.
cards.question: How can you share the truth with gentleness instead of pressure?

cards.heading: Inviting Too Soon
cards.scriptureText: I have become all things to all people.
cards.body: Inviting people without building a relationship may lead to disconnection. Build trust first before inviting them to church or groups.
cards.question: How can you strengthen your relationship before inviting someone?

cards.heading: Being Unintentional
cards.scriptureText: Be very careful, then, how you live.
cards.body: Ignoring new people or disciples can make them feel unwelcome. Discipleship requires intentional care and attention.
cards.question: How can you be more intentional with the people you disciple?

cards.heading: Losing Consistency
cards.scriptureText: Let us not become weary in doing good.
cards.body: Starting strong but not continuing leads to weak discipleship. Growth requires consistency and commitment.
cards.question: What helps you stay consistent in your discipleship?

cards.heading: Talking Too Much
cards.scriptureText: Sin is not ended by multiplying words.
cards.body: Long and overwhelming sharing can cause people to lose interest. Keep the message clear, simple, and focused.
cards.question: How can you communicate more clearly and simply?

cards.heading: Being Too Shy
cards.scriptureText: God gave us a spirit not of fear but of power.
cards.body: Fear and insecurity can stop you from discipling others. Trust that God will give you the courage and wisdom you need.
cards.question: What fear is holding you back from discipling others?

cards.heading: Depending on Materials Only
cards.scriptureText: You are a letter from Christ... written with the Spirit of the living God.
cards.body: You don’t always need materials to share. Your life, testimony, and experience with God are powerful tools.
cards.question: How can you use your personal testimony in sharing?

cards.heading: Being Unprepared
cards.scriptureText: Do your best to present yourself to God as one approved.
cards.body: Lack of preparation leads to ineffective sharing. Study and be ready to present the gospel clearly.
cards.question: How can you better prepare yourself to share the gospel?

cards.heading: Praying Too Long
cards.scriptureText: Do not keep on babbling like pagans.
cards.body: Long and complicated prayers can overwhelm new believers. Keep prayers simple and meaningful.
cards.question: How can you make your prayers simple and sincere?

cards.heading: Thinking “I Can’t Do It”
cards.scriptureText: I can do all this through him who gives me strength.
cards.body: Doubt can stop you from stepping out in faith. God equips you with everything you need to share His Word.
cards.question: What step of faith can you take this week?

cards.heading: Taking the Credit
cards.scriptureText: I planted the seed, Apollos watered it, but God has been making it grow.
cards.body: Discipleship is God’s work, not ours. Avoid pride and always give glory to God for transformation.
cards.question: How can you stay humble in discipleship?

cards.heading: Giving Up Too Easily
cards.scriptureText: So that you will not grow weary and lose heart.
cards.body: Discipleship requires perseverance. Do not give up on people, God never gave up on you.
cards.question: How can you stay committed even when progress is slow?

cards.heading: Comparing Results
cards.scriptureText: Each one should test their own actions.
cards.body: Discipleship is not a competition. Focus on faithfulness, not numbers.
cards.question: How can you focus on faithfulness instead of comparison?

cards.heading: Being Too Familiar Too Fast
cards.scriptureText: Seldom set foot in your neighbor’s house.
cards.body: Respect boundaries and allow trust to grow naturally. Avoid forcing closeness too quickly.
cards.question: How can you build trust in a healthy way?

cards.heading: Next Steps
cards.scriptureText: Do not merely listen to the word... do what it says.
cards.body: Reflect on these mistakes and grow from them. Discipleship improves as you continue learning and applying God’s principles.
cards.question: Which mistake do you need to work on the most?
